meta.basis: The alb is 'tied at the waist with a cincture unless it is made so as to fit even without such' (GIRM 336; also GIRM 119). The GIRM gives no form or colour. A cord of linen with tassels at its ends is the traditional cincture, white here with the alb; its symbolism of watchfulness comes from 'Sint lumbi vestri praecincti' (Catholic Encyclopedia, 'Cincture'), Lk 12:35, the excerpt, from the Gospel of Saint Raymond of Penyafort (7 January). The oil lamp beside it is the verse's other half.
